status: draft -03 text; held for ratification with -03
inputs: controller_bindings and binding_revocations are delivered beside the containing Bundle.

cases.description: responder-a's root record carries neither signature nor key_id. Its Capsule ID recomputes from its content and its own membership proves it under responder-a's signed checkpoint, so its key is the checkpoint's signer (log_checkpoint) at the checkpoint's time. The binding applies to that key and responder-b's signed record key: agree, redundant.

The unsigned, logged root of the linked case, with the -02 pointer /key_id. An unsigned record has no key_id, so the pointer does not select the key read from the checkpoint: not_derivable. A -03 composer omits the pointer.
responder-a's unsigned root record in a Bundle with no checkpoint or certificate: nothing ties it to a key, so the join is not_derivable.
responder-a's Bundle proves another record of its log, and lists its root as missing, not carried. No root record is carried, so there is no record to read a key from: not_derivable.

responder-a's unsigned root record, edited after it was logged: its capsule_id still has a valid inclusion proof, but no longer recomputes from its content. An inclusion proof binds only the capsule_id, so without record identity the checkpoint signer says nothing about this content: not_derivable.
responder-a's root membership entry names another log than its signed checkpoint: not its own membership under that checkpoint, so no key: not_derivable.
responder-a's root inclusion proof states another MMR size than the signed checkpoint: no key: not_derivable.
responder-a's root inclusion proof states another leaf_index than its log coordinates: not a proof of this record's position, so no key: not_derivable.
responder-a's checkpoint JSON states another root than its signed COSE form. A key is read only through a checkpoint that verifies with every stated copy matching it: not_derivable.

responder-a's log holds its unsigned root and another record whose inclusion proof is broken. The Bundle's per-record membership fails, and that is reported on the member, but the root's own membership holds, so its key is still the checkpoint signer: agree, redundant.
responder-a's root record carries key_id but no signature: a failing producer signature, not an unsigned record. It never falls back to the checkpoint key, though its membership holds: not_derivable.
responder-a's root record carries a signature but no key_id: a failing producer signature. No fallback: not_derivable.
responder-a's root record carries a producer signature that does not verify. Stripping it would not upgrade the record: no fallback to the checkpoint key: not_derivable.

The binding is revoked by responder-b's key at a time after both root records but before responder-a's checkpoint. responder-a's key comes from that checkpoint, so its T is the checkpoint's time, not its record's: the revocation applies, unjoined, as declared. Read with the record's time, it would have applied.

Both root records are signed, and each also states the other responder's key in x-counterparty-key. The join's pointer selects that member, so it resolves in both records and selects the two bound keys, but swapped: each is not the key read from its record's signature. A pointer must select that key: not_derivable.

responder-a's unsigned root is carried, but its own membership entry is removed and it is listed in completeness.missing, while another record of the same log is proved under the signed checkpoint. The other record's proof is not the root's own: no key, not_derivable.
Both root records are signed and the join carries no pointer: each key is read from its record's signature, so none is needed. The binding applies: agree, redundant.

history-a (responder-a's History) joined on same_key to responder-a's unsigned, logged root record. The record's key is its checkpoint's signer, the History's responder: agree, redundant (same_key). A log_checkpoint key states that this key's log holds the record, not that it signed it.
